w: Known as the Grand Theatre until Jean Nouvel gutted and rebuilt it between 1985 and 1993, working with the scenography house dUCKS sceno and acoustician Peutz to reinvent it from the inside out. It remains home to the Opera National de Lyon, led since 2003 by general director Serge Dorny.
s: A 1990s Jean Nouvel gutting of Lyon's old opera house
_facts: Home of the Opera National de Lyon, formerly known as the Grand Theatre
Redesigned by architect Jean Nouvel between 1985 and 1993, with scenography agency dUCKS sceno and acoustician Peutz
Serge Dorny appointed general director in 2003

w: Tony Garnier designed this cavernous hall in 1905 as a slaughterhouse, built to process livestock rather than applause. It sat idle for decades before reopening as a concert venue in 1988, now packing in nearly 17,000 standing - France's third-biggest arena. In 2030 it swaps rock for ice, hosting Olympic skating.
_facts: Designed by Tony Garnier in 1905, originally a slaughterhouse
Renovated in 1987, opened as a concert hall in 1988
Standing capacity of nearly 17,000, third-biggest venue in France after the Accor Arena and Paris La Defense Arena
Will host figure skating and short track speed skating for the 2030 Winter Olympics

w: Inaugurated in 1994 about five kilometres east of the Presqu'ile, this is France's sixth-largest mosque, built with a library and school beside its prayer halls. It also runs ARGML, an in-house halal certification body it describes as the country's most reliable.
s: France's sixth-largest mosque, east of the Presqu'ile
_facts: Inaugurated 30 September 1994; France's sixth largest mosque
Located 5 kilometres east of Presqu'ile, includes cultural facilities, a library and a school
Runs ARGML, an association of halal certification it describes as the most reliable in France
